BZ: Naval use: BZ, spoken “Bravo Zulu”, means “Well done”. That meaning comes from the Allied Naval Signal Book, not the International Code of Signals.
F: US Navy use: on aircraft carriers, flight operations are under way.
I: US Navy use: preparing to come alongside, in port or at anchor.
J: US Navy use: I have a semaphore message to transmit.
K: US Navy use: personnel working aloft.
Q: US Navy use: boat recall; all boats return to the ship.
R: US Navy use: in port, flown by the ship with ready duty; at sea, preparing to replenish.
S: US Navy use: holding a flag hoist drill.
T: US Navy use: do not pass ahead of me.
Y: US Navy use: this ship has visual communications duty.
SUB1: US Navy use, in port: the flag officer or unit commander is absent.
SUB2: US Navy use, in port: the chief of staff is absent.
SUB3: US Navy use, in port: the commanding officer is absent.
